readout_other: Nissl infarct volume; IgG deposition; CD31 microvessel diameter; vessel painting of pial collaterals
direction_notes: Neuroprotection (reduced infarct volume and IgG deposition) was reported after LIFU compared with mock treatment; neuronal excitation or inhibition was not assessed.
safety_notes: At 3.5 MPa peak negative pressure mortality and hemorrhage occurred; no mortality or hemorrhage at 1.8 MPa and none at 2.0 MPa.

target.label: cerebral vasculature, including the MCA-ACA pial collateral niche (left parietal bone 4 mm rostral of bregma and 2 mm lateral of midline)

timing.protocol_description: Pulsed LIFU: sonication duration 300 ms delivered every 3 s (ISI = 3 s) for 600 stimulations, a total of 30 min, starting immediately after pMCAO.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Based on the results of the pilot study, eleven adult, male CD1 mice were subjected to the LIFU treatment at a peak negative pressure of -2 MPa.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Transcranial FUS was performed immediately following pMCAO procedures for 30 minutes as detailed below.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: transmitted to a 1.1 MHz single ele ment focused ultrasound transducer with estimated focal dimensions of 10.21 mm in length and 1.37 mm in diameter (H-101, Sonic Concepts, Inc., Bothell, WA, USA)
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.pressure: Mice were treated with LIFU at a peak negative pressure of either -1.8 MPa, -2.0 MPa, or -3.5 MPa and PRF = 1 kHz, SD = 300 ms, ISI = 3 s, and TBD = 0:5 ms for 30 minutes.

flags.reason: Only fourteen (safety pilot) and 23 (final study) mice stated; not all were sonicated (some untreated or mock), so the number exposed is not stated as a total.
Peak negative pressures 1.8, 2.0 and 3.5 MPa; focal pressures measured by hydrophone before experiments but the paper does not say water or through skull, so placed in unspecified domain.
Tone-burst duration 0.5 ms stated; consistent with 50% DC at 1 kHz PRF (burst rule resolved by stated TBD).
Transducer placed over parietal bone; target is cerebral vasculature/MCA territory, term chosen loosely.
